title: AHMC Seton Medical Center ranks 3rd in San Mateo County nursing homes for Q1 2026
text:
AHMC Seton Medical Center was recognized as San Mateo County’s third largest nursing home during the first quarter of 2026, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS).
The facility reported 186 available beds, which is 68 more than the county’s average for the period. The center cared for an average of 104.5 residents each day through the first quarter of 2026.
CMS assigned AHMC Seton Medical Center an overall rating of 1 out of 5, which falls below the California nursing home average rating of 3.2.
San Mateo Medical Center D/P SNF led the county’s facilities in capacity with 345 beds. Golden Pavilion Healthcare placed second, offering 239 beds.
By the end of the first quarter of 2026, AHMC Seton Medical Center had paid $41,019 across three fines and accumulated six penalties.
San Mateo County, California was home to 11 for-profit nursing homes during this time.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates show that the older adult population in the United States continues to rise even as younger demographic groups decline. Between 2020 and 2024, the population aged 65 and older grew by 13%, while those under 18 decreased by 1.7%. Over the last century, the older adult population in the country has surged from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million as of 2024.
A report from 2021 indicates nearly 28 million people in the older age group might need long-term care and services. Furthermore, projections suggest that more than one-third may eventually require nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome, executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an insurance education organization. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
